body:
Fixes #509 

Currently, the quest cape teleport is valid iff:

1. quest cape or trimmed cape in inventory, equipment, or bank
2. quest points ≥ 327 (`VarPlayerID.QP`)

To keep this check valid, we'd have to update the hardcoded QP (currently 327) whenever Gagex adds a new quest.

This PR now requires the requires the (trimmed) cape in inventory, equipment, or bank **and** every quest completed (miniquests excluded), so new quests automatically gate it.
title: Require all completed quests for the quest point cape teleport.

body:
Fixes #127 , #496 , #523 .

Combination staves were already listed as substitutes for each element they provide, but a staff was only allowed to pay one leftover rune type. The `usingStaff` flag was meant to block wielding two different staves (staff of air + staff of water). It was implemented as “a staff was used,” not “this one staff is in use,” so a mist staff plus law runes could not unlock Falador, and a dust staff plus law runes could not unlock House teleport.

Spell costs are now paid with runes first, then at most one tome. Any elemental runes still missing must all be covered by the same staff. Also recognize mystic air/water/earth/fire staves as elemental substitutes.

Tests in `TransportItemsSatisfactionTest` cover:
- Reported bugs: mist/mystic mist + law → Falador; dust/mystic dust + law → House; smoke + law → Varrock
- Negative cases: law only is not enough; staff of air + staff of water cannot cover Falador; dust alone cannot cover earth+fire
- Runes plus staff: mist still works if you also have air or water runes
- Staff plus tome: dust staff + tome of fire covers earth+fire
- Two combination staves: dust + lava for earth+fire succeeds
- Mystic air staff + fire + law → Varrock
- Two tomes cannot pay two elements (only one offhand)

PathfinderTest: `testFaladorTeleportWithMistStaff`, `testHouseTeleportWithDustStaff`
title: Allow one combination staff to cover multiple rune requirements.

body:
Fixes issue #504 

Both [Jungle bush](https://oldschool.runescape.wiki/w/Jungle_Bush) and [Jungle tree](https://oldschool.runescape.wiki/w/Jungle_tree_(dense_Kharazi_Jungle)) require an axe AND machete, so the pathfinder and bank pickup hint now ask for both instead of only one. Before, it falsely required that the bush and tree only required a machete or axe, respectively. 

Since the shortest path is a 2x bush path, it reported that only a machete is required for crossing it even though it requires an axe and machete.

Text from osrs wiki:
> Both an axe and a machete are required to chop the bush. Attempting without an axe will print the message "You'll need an axe to get through this rough jungle. You don't think it would be a good idea to continue without one you've got the level to use." Attempting without a machete will print the message "You need a machete to cut your way through this dense jungle bush."
title: Require axe and machete for Kharazi jungle bushes and trees.

body:
I also had a fun night working of snapshot testing.
I let ai take a stab at it, just to get a vibe for what it would look like.
I still need to look at a bit more to see if I fully like the solution

But I did make a interesting discovery:
our routing engine is not deterministic.
turns out that hashmaps are not stable between runs.
So the ordering of equal cost transports would shuffle between runs.
and this causes the search field (how many nodes are visited) and even the solution to change between runs.
Is a small wonder that the length stays the same(although I've not looked that far into the shortcuts the routing engine takes. Because dijkstra always finds the shortest path no matter the order that the graph is presented)

so the main solution for this is to sort the hashmap

then there is the choice for a custom snapshot format.
I wanted something that is closer to human-readable then machine readable.
if we wanted to have a stable machine readable code then we could just hash something and then we have our snapshot.
But I wanted these snapshots to have a secondary purpose of debugging / pointing us to the right direction.

I also have some thoughts on the brittleness of snapshots. in general snapshots are a very brittle type of test because it asserts everything in the output.
one advantage of this is that it give a lot of coverage, and also new coverage that was not asserted before.
the larges disadvantage is that if anything changes than the tests fails even if its "unrelated" to the test.
but I think that the tradeoff is positive here because we don't expect the path between Lumbridge and Varrock to change much soon.
and if anything changes then we want to know to check.

Lastly I decided to put these snapshots alongside the regular asserts, just to make sure that the code does not brake.
although I would expect that in the future the length style asserts will be slowly removed.

the main thinks am still looking at are:

do I like the format
does it state enough info
do we want to log more to it
do i like the location of the resources
Do i want it to have subfolder (probably yes)
what impact does the sorting?
are there more test that can use a snapshot?
do i like Pathfinder pathfinder = assertScenarioPathLengthAndGet( as a pattern where the assert helper returns the pathfinder (no I dont)
do I like the assert helpers in general...
title: Snapshot testing

body:
## Summary

Adds optional Easy Teleports label integration for Shortest Path transport display text. When Easy Teleports is active, its matching item toggle is enabled, and Shortest Path's `Easy teleport names` option is enabled, Shortest Path overlays/tooltips/plugin messages display the user's Easy Teleports destination names instead of the raw teleport option names.

Pathfinding behavior is unchanged. This only changes user-facing transport labels.

## Implementation

- Adds `EasyTeleportLabelFormatter`, which maps Shortest Path display labels to Easy Teleports config keys and falls back to the original label when no valid replacement applies.
- Reads Easy Teleports values through RuneLite's `ConfigManager`; there is no compile-time dependency on Easy Teleports classes.
- Detects the active Easy Teleports plugin through RuneLite's `Plugin#getName()` API, avoiding reflective annotation access.
- Caches formatted display labels and clears the cache when Easy Teleports config changes, the Shortest Path option changes, or Easy Teleports starts/stops.
- Stores the mapping table in `src/main/resources/easy_teleport_labels.txt` so it is not treated as a pathfinding data TSV by the repository TSV validator.

## Mapping Source

The mapping file documents its sources:

- Shortest Path labels come from `src/main/resources/transports/teleportation_items.tsv` display info values.
- Easy Teleports config keys come from the separate [`LlemonDuck/easy-teleports`](https://github.com/LlemonDuck/easy-teleports) repo, specifically [`EasyTeleportsConfig`](https://github.com/LlemonDuck/easy-teleports/blob/31e38dbedb512292b0370dc9be0f72df6cd25e1b/src/main/java/com/duckblade/osrs/easyteleports/EasyTeleportsConfig.java) and the [`replacers`](https://github.com/LlemonDuck/easy-teleports/tree/31e38dbedb512292b0370dc9be0f72df6cd25e1b/src/main/java/com/duckblade/osrs/easyteleports/replacers) classes.
- The Easy Teleports config group is intentionally `easypharaohsceptre`; that is the upstream value from `EasyTeleportsConfig.CONFIG_GROUP`.

## Fallbacks

Original Shortest Path labels are preserved when:

- Easy Teleports is not installed or not active.
- The Shortest Path `Easy teleport names` option is off.
- The matching Easy Teleports item toggle is off.
- The replacement value is missing or blank.
- The Shortest Path label is not specific enough to map to one destination.

## Coverage

Includes mappings for many Easy Teleports-supported multi-destination items, including achievement diary cape, Kharedst's memoirs / Book of the dead, Pharaoh's sceptre, jewellery, diary rewards, Xeric's talisman, ring of shadows, pendant of ates, giantsoul amulet, and unambiguous max cape entries.

## Testing

- `python3 scripts/check_tsv.py src/main/resources`
- `JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@11 ./gradlew test --tests shortestpath.teleports.EasyTeleportLabelFormatterTest --tests shortestpath.ShortestPathPluginEasyTeleportsTest`
- `JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@11 ./gradlew test`
- `JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@11 ./gradlew check`

Fixes #480.
title: Use Easy Teleports labels for transport display

body:
## Summary

This PR adds per-portal toggles for the POH Portal Nexus and fixes a bug that prevented the Marim Portal from correctly routing to the Ape Atoll bank.

---

## Changes

### Per-portal toggles for POH Portal Nexus

The existing `useTeleportationPortalsPoh` toggle controlled all 39 portal destinations as a single unit. Players commonly have fewer than 39 portals built, or prefer to reserve certain portals for manual use. This change adds a collapsed config section **"POH Portal Nexus Teleports"** (closed by default) containing one boolean toggle per portal destination, all defaulting to `true`.

**Simple portals (35 toggles):**
Annakarl, Arceuus Library, Ardougne, Barbarian Outpost, Barrows, Battlefront, Carrallanger, Catherby, Cemetery, Civitas illa Fortis, Dareeyak, Draynor Manor, Falador, Fenkenstrain's Castle, Fishing Guild, Ghorrock, Harmony Island, Ice Plateau, Kharyrll, Kourend, Lassar, Lumbridge, Lunar Isle, Marim, Mind Altar, Ourania, Paddewwa, Port Khazard, Salve Graveyard, Senntisten, Trollheim, Troll Stronghold, Waterbirth Island, Weiss, West Ardougne

**Paired portals (3 toggles, one per pair):**
Camelot / Seers' Village, Varrock / Grand Exchange, Watchtower / Yanille

**Respawn portal (1 toggle):**
Covers all 8 respawn location variants

The master `useTeleportationPortalsPoh` toggle still gates everything — individual toggles are only evaluated when the master is enabled. Under the hood, `PathfinderConfig` builds a `Set<String>` of enabled portal display-info strings during `refresh()` and filters `useTransport()` accordingly.

> **Default behaviour is unchanged** — all new toggles default to `true` and the section is collapsed, so existing users see no difference until they open the section to disable specific portals.

---

### Fix: Marim Portal destination coordinates (`teleportation_portals_poh.tsv`)

The Marim Portal destination was set to `2798 2799 0` (plane 0), which is an unreachable tile inside the Ape Atoll dungeon entrance. The correct landing tile is `2797 2798 1` (plane 1), matching the Ape Atoll Teleport spell destination.

### Fix: Add Marim (Ape Atoll) staircases (`transports.tsv`)

Without registered staircase transports between planes 0 and 1 on Ape Atoll, the pathfinder could reach `2797 2798 1` via the corrected portal but had no route down to the bank at `2780 2783 0`. Added 8 staircase transport entries (4 bidirectional pairs) covering all stair tiles, enabling the pathfinder to descend to plane 0 and walk to the bank. The standard Ape Atoll Teleport spell also benefits from these entries.

---

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `ShortestPathConfig.java` | Added `POH Portal Nexus Teleports` config section with 39 boolean toggles; updated positions of all downstream config items |
| `PathfinderConfig.java` | Added `enabledPohNexusPortals` set; populate in `refresh()`; filter in `useTransport()` |
| `teleportation_portals_poh.tsv` | Fixed Marim Portal destination: `2798 2799 0` → `2797 2798 1` |
| `transports.tsv` | Added 8 Marim staircase transport entries (4 bidirectional pairs, planes 0 ↔ 1) |
title: Poh portal nexus toggles

body: This PR is incomplete, namely UI and API is not finalized. I'm publishing it to receive feedback from others. ## Overview A common request I see from other plugin developers is wanting some way to interface with shortest path but there currently doesn't exist a way to do so. This PR proposes a potential API that can be exposed to external plugins to allow them to make requests while also allowing users to control which paths are visible and prioritize which plugin paths should override other paths. * Plugins may now use an API over the event bus to request paths * Currently uses a `HashMap` to transfer data until some form of Plugin Messaging event is added to RuneLite, a la: https://github.com/runelite/runelite/pull/16863 * Plugins can only modify their own requested paths; they cannot clear/change paths for other plugins. * For now, plugins can only request one path at a time. Any new requests overwrite the old one. * Similarly, Shortest Path currently only displays one path at a time determined by the priority list and visibility. * Shortest Path still processes requests for bookkeeping even if the shortest path plugin is disabled, it just won't do the actual pathfinding unless it's enabled. * Shortest Path attempts to respect other plugins requests and provides no option to cancel/clear plugin paths directly, only toggle visibility. * Refactored how shortest path handles path finding requests internally; all internal requests for pathfinding go through the same `requestPath` code path as external plugins. * Optimized the `startUp` and `shutDown` functions to avoid redundantly loading data in-case the user toggles the plugin on/off. * Plugin Panel shows a drag-and-drop list of plugins. Plugins higher-up have a higher priority. * Debug Overlay now shows the path owner: ### Notes * Priority list order is not yet saved. Was wondering if it should be saved at all or reset each time the client starts up * All icons for UI are placeholders until I can either make new assets or find some with an agreeable license. * Navigation Button currently uses [marker.png](https://github.com/Skretzo/shortest-path/blob/74a8f15d19c4b1138a0c09bfdb089cd93982f8c7/src/main/resources/marker.png) as the plugin's icon; open to ideas for something better to use. ### Video Demo Video demonstrates that shortest-path's normal functions still work as expected, but also that other plugins (e.x. Quest Helper) can interface with it. Plugins can be re-ordered and paths hidden via the side panel. Shortest Path still tracks request/clear commands even if it's disabled so that the data remains current the next time it's enabled. https://github.com/Skretzo/shortest-path/assets/2230152/33622cee-eed8-49d2-9b52-a416f0a0bee7 ## API This initial proposal is meant to implement the bare minimum feature-set most people want and that can be easily maintained going forward. Additional features like changing pathfinding options, drawing multiple paths, changing path colors, etc., are out of the intended scope of this PR. Plugins interface over the `EventBus` by passing a hashmap of type `HashMap` containing the required parameters. Any invalid requests or requests with invalid/missing parameters are ignored and a debug message printed. For simplicity, the API is entirely one-way communication and Shortest Path does not send responses or acknowledgements back to requesters. Here is a [working example class](https://gist.github.com/jocopa3/c3260fd3443ec2c07d9a61b915f4a3ff) that external plugins can use directly to interface with shortest path or use as a reference. Internally, the API side is handled by `ShortestPathAPI.java`. It validates that the objects received are the correct types and prints debug messages when it receives invalid requests or parameters; these messages can be seen in logs or when RuneLite is run with the `--debug` argument. ### Required Parameters There are a few parameters that are required in all events: Key | Type | Description | --- | --- | --- | `plugin` | Plugin | Required. A reference to the plugin making the path requests. `command` | String | Required. Must start with `shortestpath:` followed by the command. ### Commands * `request-path`: Asks shortest path to try and draw a path from the player's position or start point to the target point. The requested path will only be drawn if no other plugin has an active path or the requesting plugin is higher on the user's priority list than other plugins with active paths. * `clear-path`: Clears any paths set by the requesting plugin; does not affect other plugins paths. Some commands may have additional parameters as listed below. **`request-path` Command:** Key | Type | Description | --- | --- | --- | `target` | WorldPoint | Required. The world point for where the path ends. `start` | WorldPoint | Optional. The world point that marks where the path should start. If missing or `null`, then the player's position is used as the start point. `hide-marker` | Boolean | Optional. If the key exists and value is `true`, shortest path won't draw the target "marker" overlay on the world map. This is useful to plugins like Quest Helper that already draw their own world map marker.
title: Create an interface for external plugins
